subject: grad
title: GRAD. ------ INFO.DY.
description: Diagram in AE(PD)-16, second of three on book p128, paired with v2-p128-1 and v2-p128-3. Continues Braxton's diagnostic of expansion conditions: gradualism considered as a *concept* (the (c) prefix) against information-dynamics. (C)GRAD (the concept of gradualism) is crossed with INFO-DY (information dynamics): the question is what gradualism produces when crossed with information-dynamics — gradualism being the seventies' default mode of activism. CRTF-D (cross-transfer definitions) sits at the top with IST-F (isolated focus) and CRT (criticism) on the upper-center. CR-INFO-DY (circular information dynamics) forms the upper-left chain. INFO-DY is the partner. INFO-TRNS (information transference) and IF-ST-DY (infra-structure dynamics) cluster on the right output. APP-RDEF (applied redefinitions) anchors the lower-right margin. INT (intention) feeds into the subject from below-left. DYM-SEP (dynamic separation) anchors the lower-left. INFO-AF-B (information-affinity basis) sits between subject and partner on the lower bridge. Structural argument: gradualism-as-concept crossed with information-dynamics produces information-transference and infra-structure-dynamics as outputs — but infra-structure-dynamics flows to applied-redefinitions (a Braxtonian alarm: gradualism's information-dynamics produces only *apparent* redefinition, not actual transformation). The upper chain through circular-information-dynamics, isolated-focus, and criticism exposes Braxton's structural alternative: when gradualism is held as concept and crossed against information-dynamics, real cross-transfer-definitions outputs are theoretically available — but they require the criticism hub, which the prose (about seventies activism's decline) implies has been lost.
